brief.title: Why the lake turns over
brief.objective: Understand thermal stratification and why the autumn turnover controls the whole year's oxygen
brief.visualDirection: Authored for this deck; see creativeDirection.
brief.sourcePrompt: Showcase brief: Why the lake turns over

narrative: By the end a student should be able to predict when a lake mixes, because they can read density against depth.

claims.claim: Fresh water reaches its maximum density at about 3.98 °C
The metalimnion is defined by a temperature gradient steeper than 1 °C per metre

creativeDirection.name: Phase map
creativeDirection.concept: Six pictures that share one axis, so learning to read the first slide is learning to read all of them
creativeDirection.rationale: Students fail this topic by memorising three seasons instead of one mechanism; a shared axis makes the mechanism the thing that repeats
creativeDirection.geometryLanguage: Everything hangs from a vertical depth axis on the left. Horizontal position always means quantity, never decoration
creativeDirection.spatialRhythm: The axis stays in exactly the same place on every slide; only what is plotted against it changes
creativeDirection.materialLanguage: Chalk on slate: a dark field with pale rules and two saturated colours doing all the signalling

depth-axis.description: A vertical rule at x=1.55in running from 1.6in to 6.3in
depth-axis.meaning: Depth, increasing downward, on every slide

hard: The axis sits at the same x on every slide
soft: Two colours only: warm above, cold below

title: One axis, six pictures
designIntent: Teach the axis before anything is plotted on it. The emptiness is the lesson.
composition: A single vertical rule at the left with three depth labels; one sentence in the wide empty right.

text: Every figure in this lecture hangs from the same vertical axis: depth, increasing downward. Only the quantity plotted against it changes — temperature, then density, then oxygen.
If you can read one of these figures you can read all six, and the mechanism stops being three seasons to memorise.

notes: Spend a full minute here. Everything later depends on the axis being automatic.

title: Summer: three layers, one sharp boundary
designIntent: Show that the middle layer is a gradient, not a place. The bands are unequal because the lake's are.
composition: Bands to the right of the axis, sized to their real depths, with a temperature curve running through them.

text: Summer: three layers, one sharp boundary
Wind-mixed, warm, uniform. 21 °C top to bottom.
Temperature falls faster than 1 °C per metre. This is a gradient, not a place.
Cold, still, cut off from the surface until autumn. 5 °C.

notes: The kink in the curve is the metalimnion. Point at it.

sources.label: Wetzel, Limnology: Lake and River Ecosystems, 3rd ed.

title: Why 4 °C is the hinge
designIntent: The one counter-intuitive fact, given its own slide and its own chart.
composition: A wide chart in the upper half; a single explanatory sentence beneath it.

alt: Water density rises from 999.84 kg per cubic metre at 0 °C to a maximum of 1000.00 at 4 °C, then falls steadily to 997.05 at 25 °C

text: Water is densest at about 3.98 °C, not at freezing. Cooling a surface layer past 4 °C makes it lighter again, which is why ice floats and why a lake can only mix while its surface is passing through that temperature.
Wetzel, 3rd ed. The anomaly is a property of the hydrogen bond, not of the lake.

notes: Ask them to predict what happens to a surface layer cooled from 6 °C to 2 °C before you explain it.

sources.label: Wetzel, Limnology: Lake and River Ecosystems, 3rd ed.

title: Turnover is a change of state
designIntent: Two columns and one arrow. The event is a transition, not a month in the calendar.
composition: Two depth columns side by side, stratified on the left and uniform on the right, with a single arrow between.

text: Turnover is a change of state
Once the surface is as dense as the deep water, a light wind mixes the whole column. Nothing about the season causes this. The density does.

notes: Stress that November is a consequence, not a cause.

title: What mixing does to oxygen
designIntent: Connect the mechanism to the consequence anyone cares about: fish.
composition: Two series on one depth-shaped chart, wide, with the illustrative caveat directly beneath.

alt: In September dissolved oxygen falls from 9.1 mg/L at the surface to 0.1 at 22 m; in November it is near 10 mg/L at every depth

text: Through the summer the hypolimnion cannot resupply oxygen and organisms consume what is there. Turnover refills the whole column in days.
Illustrative teaching profiles from the Loch Vale series, not a single measured lake-year.

notes: Say illustrative. These are teaching profiles.

title: Three questions and you can predict it
designIntent: Hand them a procedure. Three lines, low on the page, in the order they would actually ask them.
composition: Three numbered lines occupying the lower half; the upper half left to the axis motif.

text: Three questions and you can predict it
Is the surface warmer or colder than the deep water?
Is there enough wind to move a column that is already neutrally buoyant?
Three yeses and the lake mixes. That is the whole mechanism; the seasons are just when the answers happen to line up.

notes: This is the slide they should photograph.
